items.fullText: 전국 “니켈 덜 쓰고도 성능은 그대로”…포스텍, 고전압 '미드니켈' 배터리 해법 찾았다 발행일 : 2026-11-17 09:20 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 포스텍(POSTECH)은 강병우 신소재공학과 교수 연구팀이 니켈을 적게 쓴 배터리 소재로도 니켈을 많이 쓴 고가 소재에 버금가는 에너지를 담으면서 오래 쓸 수 있는 원리를 확인했다고 17일 밝혔다. 전기차의 가격인해 및 주행거리 증대는 물론, 배터리 안전성과 수명 향상, 차세대 대용량 에너지저장장치(ESS) 등 다양한 분야에 활용할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다. 강 교수와 신소재공학과 통합과정 김선기, 배터리공학과 임수진 석사 연구팀은 미국 스티븐스 공대 김재철 교수, 다나 얀 연구원 연구팀과 함께한 이번 연구 성과는 최근 에너지 소재 분야 국제 학술지인 '저널 옵 머티리얼즈 케미스트리 A'에 게재됐다. 배터리 가격의 절반가량은 전기를 저장하는 핵심 소재인 '양극재'가 차지한다. 양극재에 니켈이 많이 들어갈수록 전기를 많이 담을 수 있지만, 값이 비싸고 쉽게 망가진다. 업계가 주로 써온 니켈 80% 이상의 '하이니켈' 양극재는 충전할 때마다 몸집이 크게 줄어들며 금이 가 수명이 짧아지는 문제가 있었다. 강병우 포스텍 교수 니켈을 60% 정도만 쓰는 '미드니켈' 양극재는 싸고 튼튼하지만 담을 수 있는 에너지가 작다. 충전 전압(컷오프 전압)을 높이면 더 담을 수 있지만, 높은 전압에서는 배터리 속 액체인 전해질이 분해돼 수명이 크게 줄어든다는 것이 그동안의 상식이었다. 연구팀은 하나의 결정으로 이루어진 '단결정' 미드니켈 양극재를 평소(4.3V)보다 높은 4.7V까지 충전하자, 전기를 약 17% 더 담아 니켈 80% 소재와 비슷한 수준에 도달했다. 높은 전압에서도 100번 충전과 방전을 반복한 뒤 처음 용량의 약 88%를 유지해, 평소 조건(약 91%)과 큰 차이가 없었다. 비결은 충전할 때 소재 '몸집 변화'에 있었다. 충전하면 소재 속 리튬이 빠져나가면서 소재가 조금 줄어든다. 4.7V에서는 소재가 카드 묶음처럼 층층이 살짝 미끄러지며 줄었다가, 방전하면 원래 모습으로 돌아왔다. 소재가 부서지지 않으니 전해질과 맞닿는 면이 늘지 않았고, 전해질이 분해되기 쉬운 높은 전압에서도 수명이 유지된 것이다. 하지만 충전량을 5.0V까지 올리자 리튬이 너무 많이 빠져나가면서 소재가 훨씬 크게 쪼그라들었다. 철사를 살짝 구부렸다 펴면 원래대로 돌아오지만 너무 세게 구부리면 끊어지듯, 소재에 금이 가며 산산조각이 났다. 조각마다 새로 드러난 면에서 전해질이 계속 분해되면서 배터리 성능이 빠르게 떨어졌고, 용량은 처음의 절반에도 못 미치는 약 41%까지 줄었다. 이번 연구는 배터리 수명을 좌우하는 것이 높은 전압 자체가 아니라, 소재가 원래 모습으로 돌아올 수 있느냐에 달려 있음을 보여준다. 비싼 니켈을 덜 쓰고도 성능을 높일 수 있는 만큼, 전기차 배터리 가격을 낮추는 데 도움이 될 것으로 기대된다. 강병우 교수는 “소재가 받는 변형을 되돌릴 수 있는 범위에서 쓰면 니켈을 덜 쓰는 값싼 소재로도 고급 소재 수준의 성능을 낼 수 있다”라며 “전기차 배터리의 가격을 낮추면서 성능을 높이는 소재 설계에 도움이 될 것”이라고 말했다. 한편, 이번 연구는 산업통상자원부 글로벌 협력 사업과 산업기술혁신사업, 과학기술정보통신부·한국연구재단 사업, 교육부 BK21 사업의 지원을 받아 수행됐다. 포항=정재훈 기자 jhoon@etnews.com

items.t: Cyber giant Infoblox confirms security incident after hackers access ‘company information’
items.d: The cybersecurity and automation giant said it's working with outside investigators to understand the scale of the breach.
items.fullText: Cybersecurity and automation giant Infoblox has confirmed a cybersecurity incident, during which hackers accessed company information through one of its technology vendors. Infoblox is a privately held cyber giant that provides companies cybersecurity and networking services, such as domain name resolution and identity and user access management. In a statement, a spokesperson for Infoblox told TechCrunch that the company is “investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.” “We immediately activated our incident response procedures, took steps to contain the incident and are working with leading outside cybersecurity experts to investigate the facts, understand the scope and address any confirmed risks.” TechCrunch has learned that the data breach involves a vendor that provides SharePoint data migration services, according to a notification sent by Infoblox about the breach, two people with knowledge of the incident told TechCrunch. One of the people said sensitive customer data was taken in the breach. According to public internet records seen by TechCrunch, Infoblox hosts much of its files, emails, and infrastructure with Microsoft, including a SharePoint server, which TechCrunch confirmed is accessible through Infoblox’s single sign-on provider. SharePoint is web-based software that companies use to share and host internal files and documents. Infoblox has not named the third-party migration vendor that was hacked, but one person with knowledge of the incident said that Infoblox has terminated its work with the vendor. The company’s spokesperson did not comment on this, but added that the company has “no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved” in the breach. items.t: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t
items.d: Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results. Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Nvidia should answer.
items.fullText: Nvidia interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results. For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia’s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang. Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees. Now, the company is facing questions about its restricted chips allegedly being smuggled into China, especially by Huang’s mistress’ company. Nvidia promised to conduct an internal investigation. Meanwhile, Huang was commanded to answer questions to Congress in a closed-door joint session with three Republican-led committees. Plus, top Democrats have also vowed to investigate the company. Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Kress should answer. Huang’s role now and going forward. Huang ran Nvidia with an iron fist, having some 60 direct reports and his fingers in everything. No one knows the company better than him. An internet petition signed by 180,000 and growing is calling for the board to reinstate him. Huang may also have been mounting an attempt to return, Financial Times reported. However, CNBC is reporting, citing unnamed sources, that the company is not in talks to reinstate Huang. So, we’ll be looking for language from the interim CEO about Huang’s ongoing involvement with the company, its search for a new CEO, and any talks to bring him back. China and Singapore. As Huang vehemently argued in favor of easing export restrictions for Nvidia chips to China, Huang said that he’s seen no evidence that its powerful semiconductors were being diverted from legit buyers to China. items.t: Apple reveals new Mac security controls as AI agents raise privacy risks
items.d: Following an October announcement, Apple has detailed new permission controls, warnings, and transparency features coming to macOS 27.3 to address risks posed by AI agents and other apps.
items.fullText: As promised last month , Apple on Monday announced changes to Mac security controls designed to protect users’ data from the growing popularity of AI agents and their apps’ demand for “full disk access.” “Before granting an app such extraordinary access, users should understand that it puts all of the data on their Mac at risk,” Apple warned in its blog post aimed at app developers. Unlike AI chatbots that simply answer questions, agents run on a user’s device where they can take actions across the operating system, files, and apps on the user’s behalf. While the tools can be useful, Apple has grown concerned about the increased risks to users’ data and privacy that these AI agents introduce. At the same time, the company has been benefiting from sales of Mac minis and Mac Studio computers that AI early adopters have been purchasing specifically to run their local AI models. To balance these competing interests, Apple said in October that it would revise some of its security settings around Mac apps. The announcement followed two notable incidents involving AI agents. In one, a journalist claimed that Meta’s Muse app read their private messages without consent; a separate report from Wired cited a flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac app that could have allowed hackers to access sensitive data. Now, Apple is sharing the changes it’s making. For starters, it’s splitting up Device Control and Data Access into two settings: System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. The changes are designed to help users better understand that selecting the first option means overriding built-in security protections. To streamline configurations, Apple says there will now also be a single method for granting permissions that involves selecting the requested app from a list. Reports began to surface online Monday afternoon from customers across a range of banks saying they were receiving error messages when attempting to perform bank transactions. Chase said at around 4 p.m. on X that “JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware system” and that it was working to resolve it. The issues had been affecting both online and in-person branch transactions. The issue was not “cyber-related,” the bank said, and did not impact the entire banking system. “Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us.” The bank said that customers still had access to their accounts and funds, but some transactions were taking longer than normal. Regulators were in touch with the big banks affected “immediately,” a person familiar with the situation said earlier Monday. They “quickly determined this was contained and service was already in process of restoration,” the person said then. items.t: California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents
items.d: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s lawsuit alleges OpenAI has created AI models without proper safeguards. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 OpenAI logo. Samuel Boivin / NurPhoto via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:52 PM EST / Updated Nov. 16, 2026, 2:34 PM EST By Daniel Arkin California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people. The suit centers on a July incident involving hundreds of autonomous AI agents created by OpenAI that attacked computer systems at Hugging Face , a separate AI company. Bonta’s office alleges the attack was “entirely foreseeable in light of OpenAI’s choice to test models it knew to be dangerous in a flawed and exploitable testing environment without proper oversight.” Bonta’s office further alleges the ChatGPT developer’s failure to secure the testing of its models created a “public nuisance” and violated California’s Unfair Competition Law, a broad consumer protection statute. In response to a request for comment, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has “undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity” since the Hugging Face incident. (In the tech industry, “alignment” refers to keeping AI models in line with human instructions and goals.) “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab,” Pusateri added. “We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.” In a statement accompanying Monday’s legal filing, Bonta said Califo

items.t: U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips in foreign data centers
items.d: The Commerce Department further restricted the sale of American AI chips, addressing concerns about how Chinese companies might evade U.S. export restrictions.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips through foreign data centers The Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday morning that it would clamp down on the sale of chips to data center customers in Southeast Asian countries. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced questions in recent months about why the department's Entity List had not been updated for over a year. Alex Brandon / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:44 PM EST By Jared Perlo The Commerce Department moved to further restrict the sale of top-tier American AI chips Monday morning, addressing mounting concerns about how companies in China and other countries might evade American export restrictions by taking advantage of longstanding loopholes. As part of a new rule, data center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil must now receive a special license from the Commerce Department in order to buy advanced AI chips from American companies such as Nvidia or AMD. Over the past several years, businesses in those countries have bought billions of dollars worth’ of high-end chips, raising concerns that some chips might be illegally smuggled into China. The rule, issued by the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, will also require existing overseas data center customers to receive a similar license if they provide “significant volumes” of computing power to companies whose headquarters are in China, Russia, Cuba or other countries banned from receiving certain types of advanced American technology. Companies in these countries have allowed Chinese businesses to access their most advanced AI chips remotely , skirting rules that prevented Chinese companies from accessing these chips on Chinese territory. items.t: OpenAI will embed safety researchers to investigate AI subversion
items.d: OpenAI will embed six Apollo Research evaluators to investigate whether its AI models engage in subversive behavior, but restrictions on access and disclosure raise questions about their independence.
items.fullText: OpenAI will embed safety evaluators from Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR, and Transluce in its organization as part of a pilot, OpenAI said Monday. The news follows a series of safety incidents, including one in which an OpenAI agent swarm broke out of its sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face during cybersecurity testing. Many AI safety researchers, including from Apollo, have argued such an event might have been avoided if outside evaluators had been embedded within OpenAI to monitor its safety testing. OpenAI said the efforts support its commitments to rely on independent assessments of safety controls under the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. The pilots will begin at different points, with Apollo’s beginning this week, according to OpenAI. The idea of embedding evaluators into frontier AI labs first came from Anthropic , which last month started to give METR researchers employee-level access to its systems. Until recently, AI companies have only brought in outside reviewers to test models after post-training and shortly before public release. Evaluators say this is insufficient because it doesn’t allow them to test for misaligned behaviors like scheming during training or to monitor internal deployment use cases that could still pose a threat. The work with each third-party firm differs in scope. The pilot with OpenAI and Apollo will focus on investigating whether models attempt to subvert their own or their successors’ alignment or control mechanisms. In other words, they’ll be on the lookout for whether AI models try to undermine the safety rules and safeguards designed to keep them, or future versions of themselves, under human control. OpenAI recently published findings that while training GPT-5.6 Sol, it began leaving instructions for future versions of itself telling them to conceal mistakes and misaligned behavior from the user. items.t: OpenAI releases a new image classifier and ChatGPT warnings to combat CSAM
items.d: ChatGPT will ban an account trying to access CSAM content for 24 hours as a warning.
items.fullText: OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement. The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM. OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images. What’s more, the company is adding new warning screens in ChatGPT to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children. ChatGPT will show an alert to users attempting such prompts, direct users toward specialized support to stop harmful behavior, and also suspend the account for 24 hours as a warning. The app already blocks CSAM content and requests related to it. It said that repeated offences could lead to the account being removed permanently. OpenAI noted that it formed the message and guidelines around this behavior with organizations and researchers, including Protect Children , the Lucy Faithfull Foundation , and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages. items.t: Serena Williams winds down her VC firm, launches new fund, seeks $200M
items.d: Serena Williams and longtime business partner Beth Ferreira announced Monday the launch of an early-stage firm called Starfire Ventures.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 8:06 AM PST · November 16, 2026 Image Credits: Michael Buckner/Variety / Getty Images Dominic-Madori Davis Serena Williams winds down her VC firm, launches new fund, seeks $200M Serena Williams and longtime business partner Beth Ferreira announced Monday the launch of an early-stage firm called Starfire Ventures. The firm is seeking to raise $200 million in capital to back AI-native companies that are “solving critical, underserved problems for individuals across the experience economy,” including in areas such as fintech and health and wellness, the fund said in a press release announcing its launch . This fund is separate from Serena Ventures, which Williams founded in 2022. A rep for Starfire confirmed that Serena Ventures has recently cut its last check, though a team remains to support the existing portfolio. Serena Ventures backed more than 100 companies and raised over $100 million in capital. Ferreira worked as an advisor and general partner at Serena Ventures and has co-invested with Williams since 2015 when they backed MasterClass’ seed round. This new firm, Starfire, is a continuation of that business partnership, with Williams saying in the press release that it was “designed to live beyond” them and that the goal remains to broaden “access to capital” and create “opportunities for more people to participate in the ownership and growth of transformative businesses.” This piece and headline were updated Topics In Brief , Serena Williams , Venture 2027 San Francisco Get an Early Peek at the Next TechCrunch Disrupt Disrupt, Startup Battlefield, and more will return next year, and you can be at the front of the line. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. items.t: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
items.d: Under the interim rule, the U.S. will require firms to get licenses to export AI chips if they may provide compute to China or other restricted countries.
items.fullText: The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S. export controls by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries. Under the interim rule , the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries. The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others. The U.S. already has rules requiring chip companies to get a license to ship AI chips to companies based in, or owned by any business in, this group of countries. “This new control is a logical extension of existing controls,” the interim rule reads. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.” The move comes days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy linked to one of the chipmaker’s customers. The U.S. government has reportedly been wanting to put that customer, Megaspeed, on a special entity list, as it believes the company has been buying thousands of Nvidia chips to provide compute to Chinese businesses to get past existing export-control restrictions. Reuters reported last week that Chinese AI companies are rushing to secure computing capacity overseas amid fears of tighter restrictions from the U.S. The rule applies to data centers or any network that can supply over 12 million total processing performance (TPP), an export-control metric the U.S. uses to measure computing power. items.fullText: AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner Health systems and startups are using the latest AI technologies to support clinicians, streamline workflows and improve patient care. November 13, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients. Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI outputs and guiding decisions, while NVIDIA technologies provide the compute behind the applications. Read on to learn how healthcare teams are using AI to improve and speed patient care. Monday, Nov. 16, 8:00 a.m. PT 🔗 Artisight Helps Nurses Prevent Patient Falls With In-Room AI Device Roughly 700,000 to 1 million patients fall in U.S. hospitals each year. A fall with injury costs over $14,000 on average and can add days to a patient’s hospital stay. Artisight’s All-in-One device alerts nurses when a patient at high risk of falling starts to get out of bed. The early warning gives nurses time to reach the patient before they stand — meaning fewer injuries, shorter hospital stays and lower bills for patients, while saving nurses about five hours per unit per day to focus on other care tasks. The device uses audio and video to capture data about a patient’s movement that can be used to recognize when a patient moves towards the edge of the bed. When the patient starts to get out of bed, it alerts staff and automatically timestamps and charts the alert. Each device runs an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX , a compact edge computer, to process audio, video and movement in the room. BBW 쥐트헤센은 특수교육 직업훈련과 취업, 자립을 돕는 교육기관이다. 현재 약 500명의 청년이 30개 이상의 직종에서 직업훈련을 받고 있으며, 약 250명이 진로 탐색 프로그램에 참여하고 있다. BBW 쥐트헤센은 수년간 삼성전자 디스플레이를 직업교육과 진로 탐색 프로그램은 물론, 교직원 세미나와 회의 등 다양한 교육·업무 환경에서 활용해 왔다. 이번에 전달된 Flip Pro 전자칠판(WMFX 시리즈)역시 청년들의 직업교육과 디지털 역량 강화를 지원하는 데 활용될 예정이다. 독일 뉴스룸 기사 원문 보기 삼성전자 뉴스룸의 직접 제작한 기사와 이미지는 누구나 자유롭게 사용하실 수 있습니다. 그러나 삼성전자 뉴스룸이 제공받은 일부 기사와 이미지는 사용에 제한이 있습니다. 삼성전자 뉴스룸 콘텐츠 이용에 대한 안내 바로가기 해외소식 더보기 다운로드 닫기 다운로드 할 자료가 없습니다. 본문 복사하기 본문이 복사되었습니다. 공유하기 닫기 페이스북 X 링크드인 카카오톡 메일 라인 복사할 주소 주소복사
